title: Point sections and constant-sheaf reconstruction
statement: Fix $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $n\ge1$ in the point setting [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point]. Put $(R,B)=(A_{E,n},(A_{E,n})_s)$ or $(\mathcal O_E,\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,s})$. For an $R$-module $M$ let $\underline M$ be its constant sheaf on $s_{\mathrm{proet}}$ and put $L_R(M)=B\otimes_{\underline R}\underline M$, using the sheaf tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Apply $L_R$ and $\Gamma(s,-)$ termwise to complexes. Assume these functors are exact and $\Gamma(s,B)=R$ through the constant-value map. Use their explicit adjunction, sending $h:L_RM\to F$ to $(m\mapsto h_s(1\otimes m))$, with inverse $t\mapsto(b\otimes m\mapsto b\,t(m)|_U)$ over each object $U$. For every bounded finite-cohomology complex $c$ over $A_{E,n}$, or bounded finitely generated-cohomology complex $c$ over $\mathcal O_E$, its adjunction unit $c\to\Gamma(s,L_Rc)$ is a quasi-isomorphism and $L_Rc$ belongs to $D^b_c(s,R)$ [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility, def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]. In the integral case $c$ has a bounded finite-projective representative $P$ [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex], and $L_RP$ is a constructible representative of $L_Rc$. For every $C\in D^b_c(s,R)$ with $c=\Gamma(s,C)$, the actual adjunction counit $L_Rc\to C$ is an isomorphism. These units and counits are natural in $c$ and $C$.

source.place: second sentence ('The displayed identification of $D_s$ is then the definition of $C^\vee$ ..., $R\mathcal Hom$ at the point being computed over the coefficient ring by [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]'): point-category identification by sections and extension of scalars

proof.text: Use the displayed adjunction of the statement. Its unit is $m\mapsto1\otimes m$ and its counit is evaluation $b\otimes x\mapsto b\,x|_U$. The tensor and constant-sheaf definitions give these maps on local generators; balancing and sheafification make them well-defined. The two triangle identities hold on $m$ and $b\otimes m$, hence as sheaf maps. Exact-functor derived factorization applies to both functors by the assumed exactness. Apply the unit and counit termwise and localize: their naturality equations, including naturality with inverses of quasi-isomorphisms, and their triangle identities persist. Thus these are the actual derived adjunction maps. We use throughout that exact functors commute with cohomology.

source.place: Second sentence: extension/sections identification; exact localization expanded by the agent.

proof.text: First take $R=A_{E,n}$, so $B=\underline R$. The coefficient DVR has finite residue field; its filtration by $(\varpi_E^j)$ has successive quotients isomorphic to that residue field by $a\mapsto\varpi_E^j a$, so $R$ is finite. For a finite $R$-module $M$, choose a finite generating set and a surjection $R^b\to M$. Its kernel is a finite set, since $R^b$ is finite; taking all kernel elements as generators gives $R^a\to R^b\to M\to0$ with $a,b$ finite. On finite free modules the unit is the identity under $\Gamma(s,B)=R$. Naturality gives a morphism of this presentation to its image under the exact functor $\Gamma L_R$; taking cokernels proves the unit for $M$. The sheaf tensor unit identifies $L_RM$ with $\underline M$. This is locally constant on the single stratum $s$, with finite stalk $M$ by the constant-stalk lemma, so is constructible.

source.place: Finite-stage reconstruction: finite presentations and the single-stratum constructibility definition.

proof.text:
For a constructible finite-stage sheaf $F$, finite-ring constructible comparison writes $F\cong
u_s^*G$ with $G$ constructible on $s_{\mathrm{Et}}$. The algebraically closed-point theorem identifies $G$ canonically with the constant sheaf of $G(s)$. This identification respects addition and every scalar endomorphism by its naturality for those maps, so is an $R$-module identification. The comparison definition gives $(
u_{s,*}F)(s)=F(s)$, and the comparison unit gives $G\cong
u_{s,*}
u_s^*G$; hence $G(s)=F(s)$. Pullback takes a constant sheaf to the constant sheaf with the same value: indeed maps from either to a sheaf $H$ are exactly maps from that value to $H(s)$, by the two adjunctions and the displayed formula for $
u_{s,*}$. Consequently $\underline{F(s)}	o F$ is an isomorphism. Its local formula is $x\mapsto x|_U$, so after $L_RM=\underline M$ it is precisely the evaluation counit.

source.place: Tags 09AK (lemma-compare-constructible), 099Y (lemma-compare-locally-constant); algebraically closed-point description as recorded in the cited node.

proof.text: For $c$ with bounded finite cohomology, exactness identifies $\mathcal H^i(L_Rc)$ with $L_RH^i(c)$, which is constructible by step 2 and zero outside the same interval. Thus $L_Rc\in D^b_c(s,R)$. On cohomology the unit is the module unit of step 2, hence is invertible by the cohomological isomorphism criterion. For $C\in D^b_c(s,R)$, point-sections finiteness gives bounded finite cohomology for $\Gamma(s,C)$. On cohomology its counit is the sheaf counit of step 3, again an isomorphism. The same criterion proves the actual finite-stage derived counit invertible. In particular, a finite-stage constructible complex with zero sections is zero.

source.place: Derived finite-stage reconstruction; cohomology upgrade of the previous two steps.

proof.text: Now $R=\mathcal O_E$. The valuation-ring lemma makes $R$ a DVR and a PID; the PID lemma makes it Noetherian. For any finitely generated $R$-module $M$, the finite-free-resolution lemma supplies a surjection $R^{b}\to M$ whose kernel $N$ is the image of a finite free module, hence finitely generated. It is torsion-free: a nonzero scalar annihilating an element of $N\subset R^b$ annihilates all its coordinates in the domain $R$, so that element is zero. The DVR torsion-free lemma makes $N$ finite free. Thus $0\to N\to R^b\to M\to0$ is a bounded finite-projective resolution. Apply perfect-cohomology assembly to the bounded finitely generated cohomology of $c$. By the definition of perfectness, $c$ has a bounded finite-projective representative $P$. This argument includes $M=0$ and the zero complex.

source.place: Tags 0AUW (lemma-dedekind-torsion-free-flat), 066U (lemma-cohomology-perfect); finite free resolutions: algebra.tex Tag 00LP.

proof.text: The scheme $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ is noetherian and has dimension zero, and $\ell$ is invertible in $k$. Apply the integral stratified-perfect characterization with the single stratum $s$, its identity cover, and the perfect complex $P$ of step 5. The constant sheaf of each term of $P$ is a direct summand of a finite free $\underline R$-module sheaf, so tensor with it is exact. The bounded-flat K-flat lemma therefore applies to $\underline P$, and its ordinary tensor computes the derived tensor, so $L_RP=B\otimes_{\underline R}\underline P$ satisfies condition (ii) there. The characterization supplies membership in exactly the integral category of the statement, with completeness, compatible finite-stage étale origins and a uniform interval for reductions. The interval can be taken to contain the degrees of $P$, since its reduction has those same term degrees. Exactness gives $L_RP\cong L_Rc$. On a finite free module the integral unit is the identity under $\Gamma(s,B)=R$. A finite projective module is a direct summand of a finite free module; naturality with its inclusion and projection restricts this identity to that summand. The unit is therefore an isomorphism termwise on $P$, and by naturality and exact derived factorization also for $c$.

source.place: Proposition 6.6.11; Proposition 6.8.11(3); single-stratum perfect model and the explicit uniform-bound clause in the cited characterization.

proof.text: Let $C\in D^b_c(s,R)$ and $c=\Gamma(s,C)$. Sections finiteness places $c$ in the module category required in step 5. By step 6, $L_Rc$ is integral constructible and its unit $\eta_c$ is invertible. The triangle identity $\Gamma(\epsilon_C)\circ\eta_c=\mathrm{id}_c$ implies that $\Gamma(\epsilon_C)$ is invertible. Let $K$ be a cone of the actual counit $\epsilon_C:L_Rc\to C$. Cone-closure in the stratified-perfect characterization gives $K\in D^b_c(s,R)$. Exactness of sections and the cohomology long exact sequence give $\Gamma(s,K)=0$. For each $n$, the sections/reduction comparison applies to this $K$ and yields $\Gamma(s,K\otimes_R^L A_{E,n})\cong\Gamma(s,K)\otimes_R^L A_{E,n}=0$. Each reduction is bounded constructible by the integral definition, so step 4 forces it to be zero. In the derived-completeness triangle of $K$, both products of reductions are now zero. Its cohomology long exact sequence gives $H^i(K)=0$ for every $i$; the cohomological criterion gives $K=0$. The cone triangle and that same exact sequence then make every $H^i(\epsilon_C)$ invertible, so $\epsilon_C$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Integral counit: triangle identity, sections/reduction comparison, finite reconstruction, and the completeness triangle.

proof.text: For a module-complex map $f:c\to c'$, the units satisfy $\Gamma L_R(f)\circ\eta_c=\eta_{c'}\circ f$; for a sheaf-complex map $g:C\to C'$, evaluation gives $g\circ\epsilon_C=\epsilon_{C'}\circ L_R\Gamma(g)$ on every local generator $b\otimes x$. These equations hold before localization and hence also for inverses of quasi-isomorphisms and their composites. They prove the requested naturality on the two derived categories, independently of any presentation or perfect representative chosen in the proof.

source.place: Naturality of the displayed unit and counit formulas.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q18-4be1d0d18 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read all 8 steps of the split, every cited node's statement, the blueprint place (second sentence of lem-pod-point-dualizing-complex.proof.md), Stacks 09AK, 099Y, 00LP, 0AUW(3), 066U and 06YQ at their labels, and Bhatt–Scholze Prop. 6.6.11 and 6.8.11(3). The coefficient categories are exactly the item's: in the integral case B is the completed sheaf (completed O_E sheaf on s), never the discrete constant sheaf. The comparison to def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed goes only through the explicit 'describes exactly' clause of the stratified-perfect characterization. Steps: (1) the explicit adjunction descends because both functors are exact, which the item assumes. (2) A_{E,n} is finite, a finite presentation gives the unit, and L_R M is constant with stalks M, hence constructible. (3) Finite-ring constructible origin, constancy on the algebraically closed point, and the finite comparison unit show the evaluation counit is an isomorphism; the triangle-identity check agrees. (4) The cohomology criterion gives the derived finite stage, so a constructible complex with zero sections is zero. (5) Over the DVR/PID, the 2-term finite-free resolution plus perfect-cohomology assembly gives P; I checked the torsion O_E/varpi^a case. (6) On the single stratum, the bounded flat complex is K-flat, which is condition (ii) of the characterization; the unit on projective summands is natural. (7) Triangle identity, cone closure, the sections/reduction comparison at N=K, step 4 and the completeness triangle give K=0. This also holds under the blueprint_update wording of def-weil-derived-complete. (8) Naturality is genuinely elementary. All hypotheses hold where used: Lambda finite; s noetherian, of dimension 0, with ell invertible; boundedness for K-flatness. The delivery adds no new nodes, has no cycle (transitive walk checked), uses single-backslash TeX, keeps every step under 2000 characters, and uses no SGA source. Route: every proof dependency is on the transitive route of sk-thm-sf-package except lem-pod-point-sections-derived-reduction (sk-thm-sf-compatibility).
